response.text:
I can’t see your support data, so I can’t give the actual share. Quick options so you can drop a defensible ballpark in your deck:

1) Fast check in your ticket system
- Search last-quarter tickets for keywords/tags: "SSO", "single sign-on", "SAML", "OAuth", "login", "identity".
- Divide SSO hits by total tickets.

2) Quick sampling (if you can’t run a full query)
- Randomly sample 100–200 tickets from the quarter, count how many are SSO-related.
- Estimate = (SSO count) / (sample size).
- 95% margin of error ≈ 1.96 * sqrt(p*(1-p)/n). Example: if 12 of 100 are SSO → 12% ± ~6.4% (95% CI). If 24 of 200 → 12% ± ~4.5%.

3) If you need a single placeholder now
- Use 10% and label it “approximate/placeholder — to be verified.” (Typical ranges vary widely by product; 5–20% is common in identity-heavy apps.)

If you want, tell me how many total tickets you had last quarter and whether you can run a keyword search or random sample, and I’ll show the simplest query or sampling plan.
